name: incident_severity

question.instructions: Rate the incident's severity by combining its impact, its scope and whether it is resolved. Impact: none (no user-facing effect), degraded (slow or partly broken), outage (a feature or service unavailable), or data loss/security breach. Scope: one customer or internal only, some customers, or most/all customers. An incident with no user-facing effect is 'none' whatever else. Otherwise add impact (degraded 1, outage 2, data loss/breach 3) and scope (one/internal 0, some 1, most/all 2): a total of 1-2 is minor, 3 is major, 4-5 is critical; an unresolved incident is one level higher (at most critical).

notes: compound_judgment: the level is a rule over three facts scattered in the report (impact, scope, resolved). Generated with balanced levels, each from a uniformly chosen consistent combination. Predicted: a linear readout of pooled features can't compute the rule, so the understudies should not graduate (correctly abstaining); 'none' vs the rest may be learnable but fails the minority bar.
